assertion.rationale: F11 is now CLOSED (Task 14): Action.OpenUrl.url and Image.url in AdaptiveCardView.tsx are constrained by an /^https?:\/\//i allowlist (rejects javascript:, case-varied and whitespace-padded variants, data:, vbscript:; the fallback UnsupportedElement renders instead of a dropped/blank element), both nginx templates now emit a Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', required because Fluent UI v9's Griffel injects CSS-in-JS with no nonce wired up; connect-src scoped to Direct Line's REST+websocket host, the directline-token Function's default hostname, and the Application Insights Web SDK's config/ingestion hosts — verified in a real browser against the built bundle, not just read off the template, including the negative case: the brief's originally suggested CSP was verified to break both the Ask tab's token fetch and all Griffel-based styling) plus X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy, and both frontend Dockerfiles now drop to USER nginx (verified against the actual nginx.org Alpine package contents, not assumed, for the base image's pid path, /etc/nginx/conf.d writability, and the non-existent /var/cache/nginx). This control's only remaining open contributor is F12: the SQL dialect gate's comment-nesting logic is dialect-unaware (SQLite does not nest, T-SQL does), so a crafted unterminated comment or quote causes scrubSql to swallow the tail of a query past where the semicolon and forbidden-verb scans look; not exploitable today only because db.prepare() compiles a single statement, and lakehouse.ts already calls db.exec/db.run three lines away — one refactor from losing that incidental protection.

recommendation: F11's remediation is done; a regression here (a new Action/element with an unguarded url, or a CSP relaxation) would reopen this control. Outstanding for F12 (Task 15): make scrubSql return a structural-validity flag and reject any statement ending in an unclosed comment, quote, backtick or bracket, with comment nesting made dialect-aware (SQLite non-nesting vs T-SQL nesting).
